translations.text: At first, when King Alexander drove out the descendants of the children of Lot and forced them into the land of Kedar,
he saw fierce peoples, the Bun-Turks, settled along the river Mtkvari in four cities, with their villages:
the city of Sarkine, Kaspi, Urbnisi and Odzrakhe, and their fortresses: the great fortress of Sarkine, Uplistsikhe of Kaspi, and the fortresses of Urbnisi and Odzrakhe.
Alexander was amazed, and he learned that they were of the race of the Jebusites. They ate every kind of flesh and had no graves; they ate their dead.
The king could not make war on them, and he went away.
Then warlike peoples came, the Hons, who had been driven out by the Chaldeans. They asked the lord of the Bun-Turks for land in return for tribute, and they settled at Zanavi.
The land they held in return for tribute (kharki) is called Kherki.
Some time later Alexander, king of all the earth, came. He destroyed these three cities and their fortresses and put the Hons to the sword.
But he fought against the city of Sarkine for eleven months. He camped on the west side of Sarkine, planted a vineyard, and brought a canal out from the Ksani,
and he settled men there, Meruvians [?], at the dastagi [?] of the canal; and that place is called Nastagisi.
Then he took Sarkine: the people themselves abandoned it and fled. King Alexander had with him Azo, son of the king of Arian-Kartli,
and he gave him Mtskheta as his seat and set his borders at Hereti, the Egrisi river, Armenia and the mountain of Tsroli. Then he departed.
This Azo went to his father in Arian-Kartli and brought back eight households and ten households of foster-fathers. He settled in Old Mtskheta, and he had with him idols as gods: Gatsi and Ga.
1. This Azo, son of the king of the Arian-Kartvelians, was the first king in Mtskheta, and he died.
2. After him Parnavaz was established. He set up a great idol on the cliff and gave it the name Armazi. He built a wall on the side facing the river, and it is called Armaz.
3. After him Saurmag became king. He set up the idol Ainina on the road and began building Armazi.
4. After him Mirvan reigned. He set up Danina on the road in front, and he built Armazi.
5. Parnajob reigned. He set up the idol Zaden on the mountain and built a fortress.
6. Arsok reigned and built walls for the city.
7. Arik reigned. He built the inner fortress at Armazi.
8. Bratman reigned. Under him a city was begun in upper Mtskheta.
9. Mirean reigned, and he built the city of Mtskheta.
10. Arsuk reigned. He seized Kaspi and organized Uplistsikhe.
11. Rok reigned. He separated Mtskheta from himself by means of [?]. The kingdom was divided in two, and two kings ruled, one on that side and one on this side.
12. Kardzam reigned at Armazi, and Bratman at Mtskheta. In their times the Jews came to Mtskheta and settled there.
13. Pharasmanes reigned on the far side, and Kaoz on the near side.
14. Arsok reigned on the far side, and Amazaer on the near side.
15. Amazasp reigned on the far side, and Deruk on the near side.
16. Pharasmanes the Good reigned on the far side, and Pharasmanes Avaz on the near side.
17. Rok reigned on the far side, and Mithridates on the near side. In his time Armazi stopped being a royal seat, and the kingship was in Mtskheta alone.
18. Ghadam reigned for twenty days.
19. And Pharasmanes,
20. and Amazasp,
21. and Rev the Just.
22. Vache.
23. Bakur.
24. Mithridates.
25. Aspagur.
26. Lev, the father of Mirian.
27. Mirian.
These are the twenty-eight pagan kings in Kartli.
In the days of King Constantine, in the three hundred and tenth year after the Ascension of Christ, enemies made war, and they were badly beating King Constantine, son of Constantius.
And the emperor Constantine [the name is miswritten in the text] had lost heart because of his troubles.
There was a certain man from Ephesus, and he said before the king:
"Those Christians, the Romans and all the Indians, and anyone who holds that new law of holy Christ, defeat their enemies with power through the wood of the Cross and through their hope in it."
At that time the king set out with his troops. He sent to bring bishops from Jerusalem, Antioch, Rome and Alexandria, and he himself and his mother were baptized together with the army.
In the tenth year after that time Helena went to Jerusalem to search for the precious Cross.
And in the fourteenth year a certain woman of royal birth, named Rhipsime, fled for some reason, together with her foster-mother.
And with her was a captive, a beautiful woman named Nino, whose story Queen Helena looked into. She was a Roman of noble rank. She had made her own way, and healings had been worked by her.
And she had come to the land of the Greeks and was teaching that noblewoman Rhipsime.
And when Rhipsime fled toward the sea, Gaiane and Nino and some others with them came out into the regions of Armenia, the dwelling place of King Trdat. And they were martyred there.
But Nino remained, and she set out toward the mountains of the north and came to the river Mtkvari. She followed it and came to Mtskheta, the great city, the seat of the kings.
And she stayed like this for three years. She prayed in secret in a place covered with bramble thickets.
And she made the figure of a cross out of vine cuttings, and she stayed there and prayed. And that place was outside the city wall.
And that place of the brambles is the place of the altar of the upper church.
And in the fourth year she began to proclaim Christ God and his law: "And I found this northern land in error."
And in the sixth year she brought Nana, the king's wife, to faith during her illness, and in the seventh year she brought the king to faith through a miracle from Christ.
And she quickly built the lower church in the garden. And that pillar, which raised itself up, was made of wood.
And when they had built the church, an envoy was sent with a letter from Nino to the land of the Greeks, to King Constantine, to ask for priests. And they arrived quickly.
And the king gave Bishop John, two priests and one deacon, together with a letter from Queen Helena, an icon of the Saviour, and the wood of life for Nino.
And when they came, King Mirian, the queen and their whole household received baptism. They asked for wood to make a cross.
And the carpenters searched and found a tree standing on a rocky hill, whose leaves never fell.
And that tree was wholly fragrant and very beautiful, as if clothed with the grace of Christ. And that hill could not be reached because of the rock.
And they told the king and the bishop. And the king sent his son Rev and the archdeacon, and they saw how beautifully that tree stood.
And it was in leaf in the times of [?]. And the archdeacon recited the verse of David, saying:
"This tree is planted by the outflow of the rock, watered by dew from above, and its leaves will not fall forever."
And he commanded the carpenters to cut down that tree.
And they made the form of the precious cross as the archdeacon taught. They made three crosses from the trunk of that tree, as three bodies, and erected them in Mtskheta,
(as is written in the small, briefly composed book of the Conversion of Kartli, written by Gregory the deacon.
And King Mirian erected one cross on the mountain of the high forest, which is called Tkhoti, and that other one near the precious cross itself.
And King Mirian sent and asked for stonecutters and lime masons from the land of the Greeks.
And the emperor gave them, and they came to Erusheti and laid the foundation of a church.
And they left there the footboards of the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ. Then they came to Manglisi, laid the foundation of a church and left the nails there, and so they came to Mtskheta.
And the king began to build the church of the suburb in stone.
And when the king learned that they had first laid foundations in Erusheti and in Manglisi and had left there those longed-for boards and nails,
He was filled with sorrow and halted the work he had been pressing ahead with, until he learned from the archbishop that:
"There is with you in this city the garment of Christ, woven in one piece from the top, which those who crucified him divided among themselves,
and these men received the tunic by lot and hid it in this northern city. Their children are here now, and who knows whether they even know the place?
But its time is still to come, when it will appear in glory upon the earth. Likewise the mantle of Elijah is buried here as well."
The king was filled with joy. He immediately summoned all the Jews and asked them, "Is it truly so?" They told him the truth and did not deny it.
They said: "From here went Elioz of Mtskheta and Longinus of Kanisi [?], and Talenav [?] and Misael."
And about the tunic, they said that it had fallen to them by lot, but they denied knowing the place. Then King Mirian rejoiced when he learned that:
"The tunic of Christ had first arrived from Jerusalem at Mtskheta." He gave thanks to God and said:
"Blessed are you, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, for you desire our life and our deliverance from the devil and from that place of darkness,
when you brought your garment through those Hebrews from the holy city of Jerusalem to the city of these foreign peoples, for at the time of your crucifixion our fathers were reigning in this city."
And the king and all Kartli advanced in Christianity with great zeal.
Then the blessed woman Nino said: "Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

who sent his holy Word from the high heavens, from the mighty throne itself. He came down to earth in lowliness, to be born truly in the flesh from the seed of David, from a woman who gave birth alone [?], holy and undefiled,
which was pleasing to him. By this means he brought about our life, enlightened all that is under heaven, and above all saved those who believe in him. For he was born as a man,
was honoured as God, and was baptized like some servant of the law, from water and earth [?]. But from above he was testified to and glorified by the Father and the Holy Spirit.
He was crucified, was buried and rose again. He ascended to those same heights with the Father and is coming in glory. To him praise is fitting. Amen."
When she had said this, she took with her Jacob the priest, who had come from Greece, and one eristavi (ruler of a province). She went and stayed at Tsobeni.
She summoned the mountaineers, the Chartalians, the Pkhovians and the Tsilkanians, and preached the faith of Christ to them.
But they refused, and the eristavi drew his sword a little. Out of fear they handed over their idols to be smashed.
She went over to Ertso and stayed at Zhaleti, in the village of Edemi, and baptized the people of Ertso-Tianeti.
The people of Kvareli heard of this and fled across to Tosheti [?]. They were found later, and King Trdat brought them and baptized them.
Nino went down to Kukheti and stayed at Katsareti. She baptized the Kukhetians and the Sojians together with their people.
She went over to Kakheti and stayed at Ktseli-daba. She brought the princes of Kakheti and baptized them.
She fell ill and set out for Mtskheta. When she reached Kukheti, at a village called Bodini, she could no longer walk.
And there came [?] from the city of Ujarma Rev, the king's son, and Salome, his wife,
and his daughter, and they stayed with her as her attendants. The king and his wife Nana sent Archbishop John from Mtskheta to visit her and bring her back.
But she did not want this. Instead she commended the priest Jacob to him, saying: "So that after you he may occupy the see."

And in his presence she handed over the letter written by Queen Helena, which had been written to Nino. In it the queen, by her royal authority, had honoured her as apostle and evangelist. She had also sent the wood of life to Queen Nana.
And John celebrated the liturgy and gave Nino communion of the body and blood of Christ. She took this as provision for her soul's journey.
And she commended her soul into the hands of God in the fifteenth year after her coming to Kartli, in the year 338 from the Ascension of Christ, and in the year 5838 from the beginning of the world.
Then these two cities, Mtskheta and Ujarma, and all Kartli were shaken by her death.
And they came and buried her body, clothed in victory, in that very place, at Bodbe, in the village of Kukheti.
And King Mirian and all the people went away, for they were building the upper church in stone. And they finished it in the fourth year.
And King Mirian died and was buried by the middle southern pillar, on the north side. In that pillar there is a portion of the Living Pillar.
And in the second year his wife Nana died and was buried on the west side of the same pillar where King Mirian had been buried.
And Bakur, son of Rev, became king. Bishop John died, and Jacob, the priest who had come from the same place, became archbishop.
And in the twenty-third year after the raising of the Precious Cross, a burial canopy was made for Rev, and a tomb was built in the lower church.
And Rev died and was buried with his wife. After him, in the tenth year, this Bakur began the church at Tsilkani, and it was finished in the thirty-fifth year.
And he died and was buried in the lower church. His brother Trdat became king. The archbishop was Job, deacon of Nerses, catholicos of the Armenians.
And the king brought out a water channel for Ru[?] (perhaps Rustavi) and laid the foundation of a church. And in his time the church of Nekresi in Kakheti was built and completed.
And after him Varaz-Bakur became king. In his time the marzbans of the Persian king entered Siunik, and he withdrew to Khidari. The archbishop was the same Job.
And then Kram Khuar-Borzard, pitiakhsh of the Persian king, came to the city of Tbilisi, to the fortress.
And Kartli came under his tribute, as did Armenia, Siunik and Vaspurakan.
And in his time the nobles built the holy church in Mtskheta, and they endowed that great church with villages and estates (kardags) within Kartli.
And after him Bakur, son of Trdat, reigned. The archbishop was Elijah.
And he built a church at Bolnisi. Then he went over to the other side and restored the Armazi idols out of fear of the Persians.
And after him Pharasmanes, nephew of Trdat (his sister's son), reigned. The archbishop was Simeon.
And after him Mirdat reigned. The pitiakhsh Varash took him away to Baghdad, and he died there.
And after him Archil reigned, and the archbishop was Jonah. At that time the lower church collapsed.
And Jonah moved to the church of Gareubani and took the Living Pillar with him.
And in his time the nobles built Holy Stephen on the Aragvi. And the magi at Mogveta practiced their magian rites in the service of fire.
And in the time of that same Archil four archbishops died.
And then Mirdat reigned. And the archbishop was Glonokor. And this archbishop was also made eristavi (duke) over Kartli and Hereti by Barazbod the pitiakhsh.
And after him reigned the great Vakhtang Gorgasali, and the archbishop was Joel. At that time the Persians carried Vakhtang away.
And after some time he returned, and the archbishop was Michael. And he struck King Vakhtang in the face with his foot.
And the king sent envoys to Greece and asked the emperor and the patriarch for a catholicos.
And he gave Peter as catholicos. And with him was Samuel the monk, holy and worthy.
And King Vakhtang built the Lower Church and installed Peter as catholicos. And this was in the 170th year from the conversion of Kartli.
Ten kings had died, and thirteen archbishops. And the first catholicos was Peter.
And after this reigned Dachi Ujarmeli, and the catholicos was Samuel; and in his time people settled in Tbilisi, and they built the church of Holy Mary. And the catholicos was Peter.
And after this reigned Bakur, son of Dachi, and the catholicos was Samuel.
And after him reigned Parsman, and the catholicos was Tavpachag.
And also in his time, Chimaga, 6 [?]. And also in his time the Persian kingship came to Mtskheta, threw Kartli and its cities into turmoil, and departed.
And after him reigned another Parsman, and the catholicos was Dasabia, a native of Mtskheta.
And from this point two houses of native Mtskhetans took up the catholicosate. And in the time of that same king the catholicos was Evlale.
At that time the blessed John of Zedazeni came from Mesopotamia of Assyria; he and his twelve disciples came with him.
And after him reigned Bakur, and the catholicos was Makari. And in his time Varsken was pitiakhsh. And Shushanik was martyred at Tsurtavi.
And after him the catholicos was Samuel, and then Simon-Peter. And in the time of that same Bakur the kingship of Kartli came to an end.
At that time Mtskheta was dwindling and Tbilisi was being built up; Armazi was declining and Kala was growing great.
The Persians ruled over Kartli, Armenia, Siunik and Vaspurakan; and the catholicos was Samuel, and slowly Kartli was gathered together again.
And they appointed Guaram as eristavi, and later also as curopalates. He laid the foundation of the Holy Cross, and in his time the catholicos was another Samuel.
And the inhabitants of Tbilisi began the great church: all the people built one half and the eristavis the other half; and the catholicos was Bartholomew.
And after him his son Stephen, brother of Demetrius, was eristavi, and he built the church of the Cross.
At that time Heraclius, king of the Greeks, came through. And the commander of the fortress called out from Kala of Tbilisi to King Heraclius, taunting him as a he-goat [?].
But he took hold of his feet [?], brought out Daniel, and searched out this saying:
"The he-goat of the west will come and will break the horns of the ram of the east."
And the king said to him: "If the matter turns out this way for me, I will give you your reward."
And he left Jibgho the eristavi behind to fight. And he himself went to Baghdad to fight King Khosrow.
And a few days later this Jibgho took the citadel. He seized the commander of the fortress and filled his mouth with drachmas.
And then he flayed him alive and sent the skin after the king to Gardabani, into the land of Varaz-Grigol.
Heraclius went and destroyed Baghdad. He seized King Khosrow and made him hand over the Wood of Life.
And by his order he began to rebuild Jerusalem, and he installed Modestus as patriarch. And he came back this way in the seventh year.
And before he came to Tbilisi, Sioni had been separated [?] by the inhabitants, but the church of the Cross was still lacking.
This Heraclius sent heralds to Tbilisi, Mtskheta and Ujarma,
so that all the Christians in the cities would gather in the churches, and all the magi and fire-worshippers would either be baptized or be shot down.
But they did not want baptism, and they slyly mingled with the Christians, until he turned the sword on all of them, and rivers of blood flowed in the churches.
And Heraclius purified the law of Christ and departed. And the same great Stephen was eristavi, and the catholicos was Bartholomew, for the second time [?].
And after that Adarnase was eristavi, and in his time three catholicoi succeeded one another: John, Babila and Tabor.
And after him his son Stephen was eristavi. He separated [?] the church of the Cross and established an assembly at the Cross on the feast of the Cross, for one month.
And Stephen resided in Tbilisi, and the catholicos was Samuel, and also in his time, Evnon.
And news came that the Hagarenes had captured Baghdad. Because of this the Greeks loaded earth of the land onto a mule and carried it off to Greece.
And after him the eristavis were: Guaram the curopalates, sixth; Guaram the Young, seventh; then Arshusha the curopalates, eighth; and Varaz-Bakur, Apa [?], the patrician,

who converted the people of Garbani [?], ninth; and then Nerse, tenth; and his sons: Philip, eleventh; Stephen, twelfth; Adarnase, thirteenth; Guaram, fourteenth; and Bakurian son of Baldad, fifteenth;
and the sons of Adarnase: Stephen, sixteenth; Ashot the curopalates, seventeenth; and Guaram, eighteenth. These were the great eristavis.
And the catholicoi from Evnon onward were: Tavpachag, 1; Evlale, 2; Joel, 3; Samuel, 4; George, 5; Kyrion, 6; Izidbozid, 7; Theodore, 8; Peter, 9. These nine were married.
Then: Mama, 1; John, 2; Gregory, 3; Clement, 4; Sarmean, 5; Talele, 6; Samuel, 7; Cyril, 8; Gregory, 9; Samuel, 10;
George, 11; Gabriel, 12; Hilarion, 13; Arsenius, 14; Evsuki, 15; Basil, 16; Michael, 17; David, 18; Arsenius, 19.
Now when the holy and blessed queen Nino had completed her course in the faith of the Holy Trinity,
she who became for us the evangelist of our hearts and the healer of our souls and bodies, and set apart this one kingdom, the land of the north,

the kingdom of the kings of Mtskheta, she made everyone believe in the confession of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit; through baptism, in the coming of Christ and his birth from the holy Virgin,
the baptism and death of Christ and his resurrection from the dead, immortality and life after death, and the second coming of the Son of God to earth,
…the life of the righteous and the punishment of sinners, for His is the kingdom forever and ever, and beyond. Amen.
When [?] she came to the land of Kakheti, to the village of Bodbe, she fell ill with the illness from which she also died.
Then the kings of the land gathered, and the princes with their wives, and a great crowd of powerful people, for everyone looked upon Nino's face
as if it were the face of an angel from heaven. They wore her small, old garment to shreds, kissing it with faith and insistence [?].
All the queens sitting around her begged her, with streams of tears running down from their eyes because they were losing their teacher, the ascetic, the skilled healer of the sick.
Queen Salome of Ujarma and Perozhavri of Siunia spoke to her, and all the princes with them asked her, saying:
"Where did you come from, and how did you come to our land to be our savior? Where were you brought up, lady?
Tell us your story! Why do you speak of captivity, you who set captives free, blessed one?
For we have learned from you that there were prophets before the Son of God came to earth, and after them the twelve apostles,
and then the seventy-two; and God sent no one to us except you. So how can you say, 'I am a captive', or as in India [?]?"
Then Nino began to speak and said: "Daughters of the faith, you who are near to God, my queens,
I see in you all the faith and love of God of those holy women of old.
You want to know the ways of your poor handmaid, and I will tell you.
See, my soul has come up to my throat; I am about to fall asleep forever with the sleep of my mother.
So bring writing materials and write down my poverty and my unworthy life,
so that your children too may know of your faith and of how you received me, and of God's miracles,
some of which you have seen: on the mountains, in the bramble thicket, at the raising of the pillar, and there by the spring, up until I came here.
The Lord himself knows, and my soul knows, what my eyes have seen come down from heaven onto the earth."
Then Salome of Ujarma and Perozhavri of Siunia brought [?] the writing materials.
Holy Nino began to speak, and they wrote. She began with the story of her parents before she was born.
In the time when George of Cappadocia was martyred for Christ, in those days a certain man of princely rank, from the city of Cappadocia,
a servant of God, went to Rome to serve before the emperors and to receive a reward.
In those same days there was a certain man in Colastra who had two children, a son and a daughter. His son's name was Juvenal, and his daughter's was Susanna.
When their parents died, the children were left orphans.
They got up and went to the holy city of Jerusalem. They put their hope in the hope of all Christians, the Holy Resurrection, and gave themselves into its care there.
This brother of Susanna attained the office of [?] (devtalaroba), and Susanna served Miapor, Sarah of Bethlehem.
This Cappadocian youth came before the king in Rome. The Brangs had drawn up in battle array against the Romans on the plain of Pitalani.
God gave that Cappadocian youth invincible strength, and he stood mightily against the enemy until he put them to flight.
He captured the king of the Brangs and many princes with him, and he brought the king of the Brangs and all the princes before the king.
The king ordered that they be put to death. Then the Brangs began to weep, and they begged Zabilon:
"First give us your law and bring us into the temple of your God, and then let us die,
for it was you who captured us, so you should do this for us, and you will be innocent of our blood."
As soon as Zabilon heard this, he quickly reported their words to the king and the patriarch.
They were baptized under Zabilon's hand, and they were brought into the temple of God, the holy church, and given communion in the mysteries of Christ.
They were shown the glories of the holy apostles.
Early in the morning the Brangs rose, put on their burial garments, and went out to the place where men were executed.
They prayed and thanked God for their baptism and communion, saying:
"In death we are immortal, for God has made us worthy to see such glory and to receive the inexhaustible provision for the journey, the body and blood of Christ,
the Son of God, the immortal King, who is higher than all heights and deeper than all depths, for he is blessed forever and ever. Amen.
But woe to our offspring, fruits of bitterness, heirs of darkness." And they cried out: "Let the swordsman come and take our heads from us."
When Zabilon saw this, he was deeply moved and wept, for they had stretched out their own heads to be slaughtered like sheep, and they grieved for their children as for lambs.
Then Zabilon went before the king and begged for their release, and the king let them go with gifts.
They begged Zabilon to go with them to their land and give the law of Christ and baptism with water to all their people.
Zabilon agreed to their request. He asked the patriarch for priests and received the king's order, and they set out with joy.
When they were about one day's journey away, news arrived that the king was returning alive, with all the princes with him.
Then the ten eristavates were stirred: Kholama, Khozaba, Khlacha, Kheneshagi, Timgaragi, Zaka, Gza,
Zarga, Zarda, Zarma, and the royal Tmonigoni. They came to meet them at the great river Ghdamara.
The king divided the people and placed them on both sides of the water.
The priests blessed the river, and all the people went down into the river and were washed, and they came up by a single exit.
For ten days Zabilon laid his hands on all the people. They set up tents, the priests celebrated the service, and they gave the people communion in the mysteries of Christ.
And he dismissed the priests and set in order every rule of Christianity. And he left a blessing and went to Rome with great gifts.
And he considered in his heart and said: "Let me go to Jerusalem." And he gave all his possessions to the poor.
And that devtalari [?] had become patriarch. And Zabilon and the patriarch became great friends with each other.
Sara Miaphor said to the patriarch: "This Zabilon is the father and baptizer of the Brangs, a man perfect in wisdom and in the fear of God.
Give him your sister Susanna as his wife." And his words pleased the holy patriarch, and they gave Susanna to him as his wife.
And they went to their own city, Colastri. And I alone was born of them. And they are my parents.
And my mother raised me in her bosom, in the service of the poor, day and night without ceasing.
And when I was twelve years old, my parents sold everything they had and went to Jerusalem.
Then my father received the sign of the cross from the patriarch and parted from my mother.
And he pressed me to his breast and poured his tears like streams over my eyes and my face. And he said to me:

"You, my only daughter, behold, I am leaving you an orphan, bereft of me, and I entrust you to the God of heaven, the Father and Lord who nourishes all, for he is the father of orphans and the judge of widows.
Do not be afraid, my child! But take up the zeal of Mary Magdalene for the love of Christ, and the zeal of the sisters of Lazarus."
And if you fear him as they did, he will likewise give you everything you ask of him, whenever you want anything from him."
And he gave me a last, everlasting kiss and went beyond the Jordan to live with the men of the wilderness, and his Lord Jesus knows what became of him.
And the patriarch gave my mother as a servant to the poor, to infirm women. And I served Miaphor, the Armenian from Dvin, for two years.
And I asked her about the passion of Christ, about his crucifixion, burial and resurrection, and about his garment, the crosses, the linen cloths and the shroud, everything in order,
for there had never been, nor was there in Jerusalem, anyone equal to her in knowledge of the law, in all the way of both the Old and the New.
She began to teach me and said: "I see your strength, my child, like the strength of a lioness, which roars over all four-footed beasts,
or like a female eagle, which rises higher into the heights of the air than the male, and the whole earth, in the pupil of her eye,
is small like a pearl; she holds still and surveys it, makes out her prey, sees it like a flash of fire, lets her wings rustle, and swoops down upon it.
So may your life be, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit."
"Now I will begin and tell you everything: when mortal men beheld the immortal God upon earth, who had come from Him, Israel turned away.
And there came the calling of all the foreign nations, who served foreign gods, for he himself willed the salvation of the world which he had created.
He began to do good to the Jews: raising the dead, giving sight to the blind, and healing all the sick.
They became jealous over this, took counsel together, and sent soldiers to every land, telling people to come quickly. And they said, "Behold, we are perishing."
Then Jewish men learned in the law of Moses gathered from every land.
They rose up against the Holy Spirit, and they carried out what Christ willed of them: they crucified him and cast lots for his garment.
By lot the tunic of the Lord Jesus fell to the northerners, the people of Mtskheta. And they buried their Creator and sealed the tomb.
But he rose, as he had said before. When it dawned, the linen cloths were lying in the tomb.
Pilate looked into all this and came to the tomb with his wife. They found the linen cloths, and Pilate's wife took them.
She had become a believer in Christ, and she went in great haste to Pontus, to her own home.
After a long time the cloths came into the hands of Luke the Evangelist, and he put them where he alone knows.
But the shroud was not found, just as the body of Christ was not found.
Some said that Peter was able to take it and kept it, but that he did not tell of it openly as he told everything else.
The crosses are buried in this city, but no one knows where. When God wills, they will be revealed.
Then I gave blessing to the Lord God, and thanks to my lady for all this account.
And I asked again, "Where is that northern land, and where is the garment of our Lord?"
She said to me, "The northern land is the mountain country of Armenia. It is a pagan land under the rule of the Greeks and the Ujiks."
In those days a woman from Ephesus came to worship at the Holy Resurrection, and Niaphore asked that woman:
"Is Queen Helena also in such darkness, and is their kingdom without God?" And she said to him:
"I am their maidservant and close to all their counsels, and the Romans have a great longing toward Christ, for his faith and for baptism."
And I said to Miaphor: "Send me, and let me go before Queen Helena; perhaps she will let me come near to speak before her about Christ."
And he informed the patriarch. And he summoned me, my holy father the patriarch, my mother's brother,
and he set me on the steps of the altar and laid his hands on my shoulders. And he sighed toward heaven and said:
"Lord God of the fathers and of the ages, into your hands I commend this orphan, my sister's child, and I send her out to preach your divinity and to proclaim the good news of your resurrection;
wherever her course is pleasing to you, O Christ, be for her a way, a fellow traveller, a harbour, a teacher, a tongue of knowledge, as you were for those of old who feared your name."
He separated me from my mother and gave me a cross and a blessing as provisions for the journey. And I set out with that woman.
When we came to her house, we found there a lady of royal kin named Rhipsime. She was waiting for baptism from Jerusalem and longed to confess Christ.
Then that woman entrusted me into her hands, and I baptized her under my hand, together with forty souls of her household.
And we went to his house and stayed there for two years.

Then the Lord looked upon Greece, and in the tenth year Constantine came to believe. He confessed Christ, together with his mother and their whole palace, in the year 5444 from the beginning of the world,
and in the year 311 from the Ascension of Christ. And all of Greece turned to Christianity.
In the seventh year the holy council was held at Nicaea, and in the eighth year came our flight from Greece.
The lady Rhipsime, and Gaiane her nurse, and fifty souls set out on the fifteenth of the first month, and we came into the lands of Armenia, to the garden of King Trdat.
There they were killed, on the thirtieth of the first month, on a Friday.
But I was left behind among the rose briars, for the roses and almonds were in bloom at that time.
And as the souls of those saints were rising up, I saw a deacon coming down from heaven, in the likeness of a garment, with a stole of light.
In his hands he held a censer, from which came fragrant smoke that covered the heavens. And with him was a multitude of the hosts of heaven.
And the holy souls were joined to those heavenly hosts and rose up to heaven in glory.
But I cried out: "Lord, Lord, why have you left me among asps and vipers?"
I heard a voice from there, which said to me: "So too shall you be taken up, when that thorn which is around you has all become purple roses, made fragrant through you.
But you, arise and go to the east, where the harvest is great and there are no labourers at all."
So I set out and came to Ulopor[eti] [?], and I spent the winter there in great hardship.
In the fourth month I went into the mountains of Javakheti, to find out where Mtskheta was. And on a mountain I came upon
a great lake with an outflowing river, which was called Paravani, and I stayed there for two days.
I asked the fishermen for food, and I was strengthened by the power of that food, and I gave thanks to God.
And there were shepherds in that same place, and among their flocks they were sounding the night calls [?].
And they were calling on their cursed gods, Armaz and Zaden, and vowing them offerings "when we get back."
Early in the morning I went and asked one of them what village they were from, and he answered me:
"Some of us are from Dabi, some from Sapurtsli, and some are Kinjarians and Rabatians of the great city of Mtskheta, where the gods are gods and the kings reign."
I looked at the northern mountains, for even in the days of summer they appear full of [?] and fierce snow.
And I was filled with dread, and I said: "Lord, Lord, take my soul from me."
And I took a stone and laid it under my head as a pillow, and I fell asleep at the outflow of that lake.
And in a vision a man came, of moderate stature, with half-length hair [?]. And he gave me a sealed book and said to me:
"Arise and quickly take this to Mtskheta, to the king of the pagans." And I began to entreat him with weeping and said to him:
"Lord, I am a foreign and ignorant woman. How shall I go? I do not even know the language, or what I am to say among foreign peoples."
Then he opened the letter and gave it to me to read. It was written in the Roman tongue and was sealed with the seal of Jesus.
Ten sayings were written in it, like those on the first tablets of stone.
The first saying: "Wherever this gospel is preached, there this woman too will be spoken of."
2. "There is neither male nor female, but you are all one."
3. "Go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."
4. "A light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel."
5. "Wherever this gospel of the kingdom is preached, it will be spoken of in all the world."
6. "Whoever receives you receives me, and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me."
7. The Lord loved Mary greatly, for she always listened to his true wisdom.
8. "Do not be afraid of those who kill your bodies, for they cannot kill the soul."
9. Jesus said to Mary Magdalene: "Go, woman, and bring the good news to my brothers."
10. "Wherever you preach, [do so] in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit."
When I had read this, I began to pray to God, and I understood that this vision came from heaven.
I lifted my eyes to heaven, blessed the Most High, and asked him for help in my troubles.
I followed the outflow of that lake and set out.]
Its course ran toward the west. I took a hard and rough road, and I suffered great hardships on the way and great fear of wild beasts,
until I arrived here, where the water begins to flow toward the east. From then on I had relief.
I found travelers and reached the region of Kartli, at the city of Urbnisi. There I saw a strange people who served strange gods: they worshipped fire, stones and wood.
My soul grieved over their perdition. I went to the synagogue of the Jews because of the Hebrew language, and I stayed there for one month and studied the condition of this land.
One day great crowds, countless in number, set out from that city and went to the great city of Mtskheta,
which was the seat of the great kings, to trade and to pray to Armaz, their god.
I went along with them, and we reached the city of Mtskheta, on the far side, at Mogvta. We stopped there on the bridge and watched that fire-worshipping people.
I wept over their magian religion and their error, because of their perdition, and I also mourned my own exile.
On the next day there was the sound of horns and trumpets. A countless crowd of people came out. Like flowers they came out, awe-inspiring and terrifying. But the king had not yet [?] set out.
When the hour came, everyone fled and hid here and there, and everyone took refuge under cover, because Queen Nana was coming out.
After Queen Nana had passed, only then did all the people slowly come out.
They decorated all the streets with garments of every kind and with leaves. And all the people began to praise the king.
And then King Mirian came out in a spectacle too dazzling for the eyes to bear. And I asked a Jewish woman:
"What is this?" And she said to me: "The god of their gods, the supreme one [?], Armaz, besides whom there is no other idol."
So I went to see Armaz. The mountains were filled with banners and people, as if with flowers.
I hurried ahead to the fortress of Armazi and stood near that idol, in a crack in the wall. I watched wonders and dreadful things
that no tongue can describe: how the kings and all the people were nearly faint with terror, in fear and trembling.
I saw a terrifying figure standing there. Behold, there stood a man of bronze. On his body he wore a coat of golden mail and a golden helmet. On his shoulders were set [?] ("prtskhili") and beryl.
In his hand he held a sharpened sword, which gleamed and turned in his hand, as though whoever touched it would hand himself over to death. And they were saying:
"Woe to me if I have failed in anything toward the glory of the great god Armaz, or have strayed in any word with the Hebrews, or have been caught even listening to the magi, the servants of the sun.
Certain strangers speak of some great God of the heavens. May he not find any blemish in me
and strike me with that sword of his, which the whole land fears." And everyone bowed down in fear.
On his right stood a golden idol, and its name was Gatsi.
On his left stood a silver idol, and its name was Ga. Your fathers from Arian-Kartli had held these as gods.
Then I wept and sighed to God over the errors of those northern lands: the light was hidden and darkness held sway.
I saw those mighty kings and all the princes, and how they had been swallowed alive by the devil, as the dead are swallowed by hell.
They called stones and wood their creator. They worshipped as god bronze, iron and brass hammered out over the bellows.
These they took to be the creator of heaven and earth.
Then I remembered the word that the Patriarch Juvenal, my holy father, had given me as a command:
"I am sending you out as a mature man, and you are to reach a foreign land, the peoples Dgeveli, Zepheli and Narkadoveli, who are men hateful to God, warlike and hostile."
Then I lifted my eyes to heaven and said: "Lord, Lord, through the greatness of your power these enemies of yours will cringe before you.
It is because of your great long-suffering that these enemies, the ashes of the earth, do whatever they devise.
But do not disregard them, for man is your image. For his sake one of the Trinity became man and saved the whole world.
"Look upon these peoples too, and be angry with these invisible spirits, the rulers of the world, the princes of this darkness.
And show me, O God of my father and my mother, me, this handmaid of yours, the child of your servant,
so that all the ends of the earth may see your salvation, and the north may rejoice together with the south, and every tongue may worship you, the only God, through Jesus Christ our Lord,
to whom it is fitting to offer thanksgiving and glory, now and always and in the ages to come. Amen."
And in the twinkling of an eye, the air and the winds stirred from the west, and thunder sounded with a terrifying voice.
And a swift cloud appeared, fearful to look at. And the breeze from the west brought a [?] breath of bitterness and stench.
Then everyone fled to the countryside and to the city. And they had time to get into their homes.
And all at once that cloud of wrath arrived and brought hail, each stone as heavy as a litra, on that place alone. It smashed the idols, ground them down and crushed them to powder.
And a fierce wind tore down the walls and threw them down onto the rock, which you yourselves have seen, or perhaps not.
And the king said with tears: "Hē, hē, rait-meboy khojat stabanub rasul psarzad."
Its translation is this: "You speak the truth, blessed queen and apostle of the Son of God."
And when the wrath had died down, I came out of the cleft in the rock and found that beryl stone.
I picked it up and went on toward the far end of the rock, where the old city had been. A fortress had stood in that place.
And a beautiful [?] tree stood there, tall and with many branches. I came under that tree and marked on myself the sign of the cross of Christ. And I prayed there for six days.
When you, the crowd of the people, came out and looked for those gods that had been destroyed, and did not find them, I was there then,
for it was the sixth day of that month, the day on which Emmanuel on Tabor showed the image of the Father to the chief ones of the living and the chief ones of the dead.
Then this sister of mine, Sroshana, a lady of the royal court, came. She saw me, brought a Greek-speaking woman, and asked me about my whole journey.
Then I saw tears flowing from her eyes because I was a stranger.
When she had learned everything about me, she pressed me to let her take me to the palace, but I did not want to go, and she left.
And on the third day I came down to the city of Mtskheta and made my way to the king's garden.
When I reached the gate of the garden, there was a small hut belonging to the gardener. When I went in, this woman Anastasia was sitting there.

When she saw me, she stood up and welcomed me warmly, like someone she knew and a friend. She washed my feet, anointed me with oil, set a table with wine for me, and pressed me to eat and drink. And I stayed with her for nine months.
She was childless, and she and her husband were grieving over it. I saw in a vision that a man the colour of light came and said to me:
"Go into the garden. Under the [?] fir trees there is a small place, lovingly prepared. Take earth from that place and give it to these people to eat, and they will have children."
And I did so. And they had many sons and daughters, as you yourselves see.
And in those same days, two and three times, I saw a vision during my light slumber, resting upon my knees:
the birds of heaven would come and go down into the river. They would bathe, then come to that garden and pluck at the [?], and feed on the flowers.
And they cry out to me tenderly, as though that paradise were mine; they come around me with chirping and call out to me; their appearance was many-coloured and beautiful.
And this happened many times. And I told this to my sister, the daughter of Abiathar. She answered me and said:
"O stranger and native-born here, captive and redeemer of captives, know that that new time has come upon you, and through you that ancient report has been heard.
the deed of our fathers, the unjust shedding of the innocent blood of that heavenly man, by which God brought shame upon the Jews:

their scattering to the ends of heaven, the fall of the kingdom, the taking away of that holy temple, the winning of that foreign people, the calling of them his own, and the giving of glory to them."
And again she said: "Jerusalem, Jerusalem, how your children have been stripped from you [?]! And you will gather the peoples from all the ends of heaven under your wings."
"Behold, this woman has come here too, and she will change the whole order of this land." And she turned to me and said:
"This is the meaning of your vision: through you this place of the garden will become a paradise for the glorifying of God, to whom be glory now and always and to the ages of ages, amen."
And it came to pass that God looked in mercy upon this forgotten land of the North: the Caucasus, the highlands of Armenia, whose mountains were covered with mist

and whose plains were covered with the fog of error and ignorance. This land lay in shadow, cut off from the Sun of righteousness, from the coming and the knowledge of the Son of God, just as it was rightly named "the North" (Shadow).

This is not to say that it lacked the light of this sun, or lacks it now. Everyone under heaven sees the sun, and it sees everything. Even the places it holds back its heat from, it looks upon with its light.
That is not why this land was called "the North" (Shadow). Rather, so many years and so many generations had passed since Noah, Eber and Abraham.
And in that time lived Job the nobleman, tested by the Tempter, as were Joseph, Moses, Joshua, the priests and the judges, one after another, whom we know from hearing the divine books.

Until the coming of Christ, 5,500 years passed. From the birth of Christ to the crucifixion, 33 years passed. And from the crucifixion of Christ to the baptism of Constantine, king of the Greeks, 311 years passed.
And fourteen years after that, Nino, the preacher of truth and our queen, was sent to our land,
just as, in the darkness, the morning star rises and the dawn breaks, and after it rises that great ruler of the day.
Such was our life, O Georgians: we went about in the light, yet we dwelt in darkness. We rejoiced in pleasure while we stored up mourning, and there was no one to comfort us in it.
We served created things and not the Creator. Instead of Him who sits upon the chariots of the cherubim, our fathers worshipped high mountains: Ebal
and Gerizim. And on it there was neither God, nor Moses, nor any sign of them, but only lifeless idols of stone.
In this land of Kartli there were two mountains, and on them two idols, Armaz and Zaden, which with foul breath took in the smell of a thousand souls of firstborn children.
Armaz and Zaden. Their parents gave the children to them as an offering and sacrifice, as though there would never be death again [?]. And this went on until now.
There were also other royal idols, Gatsi and Ga. To them one royal child was sacrificed: it was burned in fire, and the ashes were scattered over the head of the idol.
After all this, I will tell you my father's account, which I know from reading books and from what my father told me.
When Herod was reigning, we heard here that the Persians had seized Jerusalem.
a letter of mourning was written to all the Jews of Kartli: to the inhabitants of Mtskheta, the priests of Bodi, the scribes of Kodis-Tsqaro, and the interpreters of Sobis-Kanani, saying:
"Twelve kings have come to conquer our land."
Everyone hurried to set out to help them. But a little later another message, this one of comfort, came from Jerusalem to the whole land, saying:
"Those Persians did not come to conquer the land. Instead of armour, weapons and provisions, they had yellow gold,
myrrh, which quickly heals wounds, and fragrant incense. Each of their horsemen had these.
Each of the kings themselves had one load of these, and they were looking for a certain newborn child, a son of David. They found him, a stranger,
the son of a stranger woman, born at the wrong time in a place that was no proper place, as is usual for those who live as outsiders.
They came to that child and worshipped him, and they offered him all these gifts. Then they crossed the mountain and left in peace.
Now do not be afraid, Jews. I, Herod, searched and did not find that child or his mother.
But now I will turn the sword on every infant two years old and under, and he will perish along with them. So now be at ease,
for all this was an illusion." Thirty years after this, the priest Annas wrote from Jerusalem to my grandfather Oziah, saying:
"That same child, to whom the kings of the Persians had come with gifts, has grown up and reached the full measure of adulthood.
All the tribes of Israel went out to the water of the Jordan, to the son of Zechariah, and your father's mother's brother Elioz was with them too. And behold, the sky thundered and the earth shook,
the mountains trembled, the hills danced, the sea stood still, the waters flowed upward, the son of Zechariah fled, and terror and trembling fell on all of us.
Because of the great crowd of people, we kept silent about this matter, which had indeed been known to God from eternity."
In the fourth year, a command came out from Jerusalem from King Herod, saying:
"To all the sons of Israel scattered across every land: see one God, take heed, and listen to one law.
Learn the one word of Moses, which he spoke: 'Whoever on earth calls himself God, let him be hanged on a tree.'
And he also said: 'Cursed is everyone who is hanged on a tree.'
Now behold, a certain man has arisen whose name is Jesus. On his own authority he calls God his Father and claims, as it were, that he himself is like God,
"Let us all come to his death and fulfil the commandment of God and of Moses."
And from here went my father's mother's brother Elioz, an old man. His mother was of the tribe of Eli the priest, and Elioz had only one sister.
His mother pleaded with her son and said to him: "Go, my child, at the king's summons and according to the rule of the law.
But whatever they plot, do not let your mind join in it at all. No, my child,
for this is the word of the prophets and the parable of the wise. It is a mystery hidden from the Jews, but for the gentiles it is light and eternal life."
And Elioz and all the Jews went from Kartli. And everything that we now know through Nino, from the Gospels, through Christ, was fulfilled.
And the garment fell by lot to this land, and Elioz brought it.
And as for his mother: when the executioner on the cross struck the smith's hammer upon the nails in Jerusalem, she heard the sound here. That woman cried out bitterly and said:
"Farewell, kingdom of the Jews, for you have killed your own Savior and Redeemer, and from now on you have become enemies of the Creator.
Woe is me, that I did not die before, so that I would not have heard this, and that I did not stay alive a little longer,
so that I might have seen the light shining forth upon the gentiles and the glory of the people of Israel." And at these words that woman, the mother of Elioz, died.
And this Elioz brought that tunic of the Savior Jesus Christ to Mtskheta, to our house, and he saw that his mother had died at those words.
And his sister came out to meet him, drenched in tears as if in blood. She threw her arms around her brother's neck, took that garment of Jesus from him, and pressed it to her breast.
And at once her spirit departed because of these three bitter things: her mother's death, and even more her pain at the death of Christ, and her longing for that garment.
Then there was a great commotion in Mtskheta among the kings, the princes and all the people.
And King Amazaer saw that garment of Jesus and wanted to take it away. But he was seized by dread at the dead woman's grip on it, and he was afraid and did not dare.
And Elioz buried his sister, and she held that garment in her hands.
And that place exists. God knows it, and my mother Nino knows it, but she does not tell, for it is not right to speak of it now.
But let this alone be enough for Nino's disciples and for the believers in Christ: the place is near that cedar which came from Lebanon and was planted in Mtskheta.
Apart from this, I heard from my father: "There is also another thing, clothed with power, the double one too, the mantle of Elijah, in this city in our hands,
under the firm foundation of the altar, among stones, uncorrupted until its time." For my mother Nino sent me many times to my father
so that I might find out from him exactly, and from his heart, the place of that garment. But he only entrusted this portion [?] to me and said to me:
"Here is his place of fasting, where the tongues of men will not fall silent in singing praise to God; upon it is that place,
like the place of Jacob, seen as a ladder and reaching up to heaven, from now on and forever, with glory and praise that never fail."
When I, Sidonia, the daughter of Abiathar, first saw holy Nino on the top of the fortress of Mtskheta, in that high tower beneath those bronzes,
[?] of the king was sitting in the cool summer places and the places of rest when the Lord shattered Armaz and the other idols by the terrible wrath of his face,
as is written earlier in her testament, until Queen Nana came to believe in Christ God as the Son of God.
The blessed, holy Nino spent six years, as she herself says in her Life, and during that time she made us seven women disciples of her faith,
for she performed many healings in secret, until by God's providence she began to heal openly.
God first showed his power through her on Queen Nana, in the bramble thicket,
and through her prayer he healed the queen of a severe illness that human skill had been unable to heal.
After that the chief of the magi, the Persian prince Khuara, fell ill. He was cruelly tormented by an evil spirit and had come near to death.
This prince was the brother of Queen Nana's mother. Then Queen Nana pleaded with my mother Nino;
and the king too was observing the matter little by little, and he said to Nino doubtfully: "By the power of which god do you do this work of healing?
Are you a daughter of Armaz, or a child of Zaden? You came here as a stranger and fell down before them, and now mercy [?] is upon you,
and they have granted you the power of healing, so that you may make your living by it in this foreign land. May they be glorified forever!
So stay before me always, like one of the nurses, honoured in this land. But do not speak that foreign word, the faith of those misguided Romans,
and do not wish to speak of it here at all. For behold, here are the gods who give great harvests and rule the world, who spread the sunlight and give the rain,
who make the fruits of the earth grow, the gods of Kartli, Armaz and Zaden, who search out everything hidden,
and the ancient gods of our fathers, Gatsi and Ga. And let you yourself serve to make people believe in them.
And now, if you heal this prince, I will make you rich and settle you in Mtskheta as a servant of Armaz. Although he was shattered by the violence of that storm, his place remains unshaken.
This Armaz and Itrushana, the god of the Chaldeans, are bitter enemies.
The one brings the sea against the other, and the other cannot bring anything at all against the first [?], as is the custom of the rulers of the world. Let this command of mine be enough for you."
The blessed Nino answered the king and said: "O king, may you live forever in the name of Christ, through the intercession of his holy Mother and of all the saints with her.
May God, the Creator of heaven and earth, the Maker of everything created, send upon you,
out of his great glory and his countless mercy, one spark of his grace, like a spark from a furnace,
so that you may know and understand the righteousness of heaven and the light of the sun, the depth of the sea and its foundations,
the breadth of the earth and its foundations, and so that it may be made known to you, O king, who clothed the heavens with clouds and the thunders with the voice of the air,
at whose fierceness the earth shakes and the thunderbolts run, and in whose track fire is kindled by his anger,
or when the great dragon that is in the sea stirs and shakes the whole earth, until the firm mountains and the rocks are broken;
And know all this precisely: God is in the heavens, and He Himself is invisible to all creation, except to the One who came forth from Him.
This One was sent to earth as a man. He accomplished everything for which He had come, and ascended to those same heights, to be with the Father.
He alone has seen the One who has no beginning, and He alone is with Him who looks upon the lowly and knows the lofty from afar.
But now, O king, the time when you will draw near to God is close. I see that there is a wonder in this city: the robe of the Son of God.
Some have said that the mantle of Elijah is here too, and there are many wonders here which God Himself has made known to them.
And I will heal this nobleman by the power of my Christ and by the cross of His passion,
just as God healed Queen Nana of her grievous illness. And what I have made known to him, he will do, so that he may enlighten his own soul and bring his people near to God."
Then they brought that nobleman. Saint Nino took him, and me, and Queen Nana into the garden, under the fir trees. She stood him there and made him raise his hands toward the east.
And she made him say three times: "I renounce you, devil, and I follow Christ, the Son of God."
And Saint Nino wept, sighing from her soul, and asked God for help for that man, and we did the same with her for a whole day.
And quickly that evil [?] (the text reads 'daughter', probably for 'spirit') went out, and he and all his household became disciples of Saint Nino,
and he glorified God, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
And one day, at the beginning of summer, on Saturday the twentieth of the month of July, the king set out and went hunting in the direction of Mukhnari.

He went around the country of Mukhnari and went up into the high forests of the mountains of Tkhoti, so that he might look out over the great fortresses of Aspa, Kaspi and Uplistsikhe, and he went up to the summit of that mountain.
And just at midday the sun grew dark above him, and it became pitch-black night. A very deep darkness covered those regions and places.

Because of that distress and calamity all his people were scattered from one another. The king was left alone, and he wandered over the mountains and through the high forests, frightened and trembling.
And he stopped in one place and gave up hope of staying alive.
But God, who does good, turned his mind from ignorance to understanding and from unknowing to knowledge. He came to his senses, reasoned in his heart and said:
"Look, I see that I have called on Armaz and Zaden with a loud voice, and I have found no relief.
So now let me call on the One whom Nino preaches, the Cross and the Crucified, through hope in whom she works many healings.
Might He not now have the power to save me from this distress? For I am in hell while still alive, and I do not know
whether destruction has come upon the whole earth and light has been turned into darkness, or whether this affliction is for me alone." At once he cried out and said:
"God of Nino, lighten this darkness for me and show me the way to my dwelling, and I will confess your name, and I will set up the wood of your cross and worship it,
and I will build you a house to be your house and a place of prayer for me, and I will be obedient to Nino and to the law of the Romans."
As soon as he had said and spoken these words, day broke and the sun quickly shone out.
Then the king got down from his horse and fell face down on the ground, sighing and weeping.
He rose, stretched out his hands toward the east and said: "You are God over all gods and Lord over all lords,
the God whom Nino preaches. Your name is to be praised by everything created under heaven and on earth.
You saved me from distress, and when I called on your name you quickly turned my darkness into light.
See, I have come to know that you want to save me and bring me close to you. Now I will set up the wood of your cross in this place,
so that your holy name may be glorified by it, and this event and these miracles may be remembered forever." He took careful note of that place, then set off and came away.
When his men saw the light, those who had been scattered and in distress for a long time gathered together again.
The king called out and said to all his people:
"All you people, give glory to the God of Nino, for he is the eternal God, and praise belongs to him alone forever. Amen."
Queen Nana and the whole city went out to meet the king, because they had first heard that he was lost, and then that he was returning safely.
They met him at Kindzara and Ghart. There was great joy because he had returned safely.
Blessed Nino, as was her custom, was standing at evening prayer in the bramble thicket, and we were with her, fifty people.
When the king came in, the whole city was stirred up. The king cried out in a loud voice and said:
"Where is that foreign woman, who is my mother, and where is her God, my savior?"
When he heard that she was here in the bramble thicket, praying, the king turned aside with his whole army. He came, leapt down from the saddle and said to Nino:
"Am I now worthy to call on the name of your God, my savior?"
The holy woman taught him and quickly instructed him to worship Christ, the Son of God, facing east.
Then all the people groaned and wept, because they saw the tears of the king and queen flowing for joy and because of the great wonder that had taken place.
The next day he sent envoys to Greece. Blessed Nino taught every person, day and night, the true way of the faith.
The king spoke with Nino about building a church. By then the king and all the people had eagerly turned toward Christianity, before the priests arrived from Greece.
The believing king said to Saint Nino: "Where shall I build a house for God?" And the blessed one said to him:
"Wherever the mind of kings is firmly set." And the king said to her: "I love those brambles of yours, and my mind is content there, but not like this,
rather, I will not spare the royal garden, the height of its firs, the fruitfulness of its [?] and the fragrance of its flowers,
but in it I will build a temple where I may pray, which will stand forever."
At once they brought timber and began to build. They cut down the fir tree and made it ready as a pillar, and on its roots they laid the foundation of the church.
And there was the terrible vision of the pillar and of its foundation, which is written above.
And when the time came to raise the pillar mentioned earlier, the builders began to raise it, and they could not.
Then a countless multitude gathered, and the king with them. They began to prepare all kinds of devices and machines. Not only could they not raise it, they could not even move it.
And all the wisdom and contrivance of men came to nothing, so that through the raising of that pillar God might be wondrously glorified and people might be more firmly established in the faith.
And since they could not raise it and the work failed, the king and all the people went away, disheartened with grief, and they were sorrowful over this.
But blessed Nino stayed in the same place, and twelve other women with her. And that blessed one lamented and shed tears over the pillar.
And at about midnight these two mountains, Armazi and Zaden, seemed to be toppling forward, as if they were collapsing, and they dammed the waters of both rivers.
And the Mtkvari burst out and was terribly sweeping the city away. And from there arose terrible and dreadful sounds of captivity and flight.
Likewise the Aragvi came down from above the fortress, and there were terrible roarings.
And the women were frightened and fled, and I too with them. But the blessed holy Nino cried out:
"Do not be afraid, my sisters. Those mountains stand where they are, those waters flow where they are, and all the people are asleep.
But the way the mountains seemed to collapse rightly shows us that the mountains of unbelief have collapsed in Kartli.
And the waters that were dammed up mean that the blood of children sacrificed to demons has been stopped.

And these cries of captivity belong to a multitude of demons, for they are mourning their own desolation, because they are being driven out of this place by the power of the Most High and by the Cross of Christ.
Turn and pray to God, children!" And at once those sounds ceased, and there was nothing.
And holy Nino stood and stretched out her hands toward heaven and lifted her eyes to God, and she prayed and entreated
that the enemy might not hinder this work of the faith, on which the king and all the people had zealously set out.
And before the cock had yet crowed, a mighty army struck terror at all three gates and broke down the gates of the city.
And the city was filled with the Persian army, and at once there arose shrieks enough to make one faint with terror, and cries, and slaughter of the people, so that it seemed blood was flowing.
And the whole place was filled, and a multitude of shouts and swords came upon us, and our flesh melted and our souls failed.
And I was weeping for my father and for my kinsfolk, and suddenly I heard them calling out loudly:
"Thus commands Khuara, king of the Persians, and Khuaran Khuara, king of kings: spare every Jew from the edge of the sword."
When I heard this I came to my senses, and I wavered, I and the ten who were with me. And the swordsmen had come near and were striking and killing all around us.
And a voice was heard loudly: "They have seized King Mirian!" And that valiant striver looked around and said: "Have they done it again? I know that he is in great distress."
And she gave thanks to God, for this was a sign of their destruction, and of the salvation of Kartli and the glory of this place.
And holy Nino comforted us like a skilled teacher, for she was truly and in very truth a teacher and apostle of Christ.
And she turned to the host that was advancing on us and said to it: "Where are the kings of the Persians, Khuara and Khuan Khuara? Did you set out from Sabastan yesterday?
You have come quickly. Great indeed is your army, you are beyond all measure, and you have mightily shattered this city and put it to the sword.
I command the winds and breezes: go to the dark northern mountains of Kedar. The One from whom you flee has come here."
And she moved her right hand and traced the sign of the cross with her hand. At once that whole multitude of people vanished, and a great stillness fell.
And we glorified God and called holy and blessed Nino blessed.
And as dawn was just beginning to break, my sisters fell asleep, but I stayed awake. And holy Nino stood with her hands raised.
And behold, a youth came and stood over us, wholly clothed in light, and wrapped in a cloak like fire.
And he spoke some three words to blessed Nino, and she fell on her face.
Then the youth put his hand to the pillar, took hold of its top, lifted it, and carried it up to the height of the heavens.
Amazed, I went up and said to the blessed lady: "What is this?" But she bowed my head down to the ground.
And I began to weep in that terror. After a short time the blessed one rose, raised me up as well, and we withdrew from that place.
The women were still at a distance. And behold, I saw the pillar coming down like fire and drawing near to its base.
And as it happened, it stood over that base, raised about twelve cubits above the ground, and slowly came down onto its own cut stump,
for its base was its own root, from which the living pillar had been cut.
And just at early dawn the king had risen, his heart weighed down with cares, and he looked toward the garden, toward his church that had been begun, for his mind was fixed there.
And he saw there in the garden a light like lightning reaching up to heaven.
He began to run, coming in haste, and the whole multitude of the people with him.
And when they came they saw the wonder: the pillar, shining with light, was coming down to its place, as though it stood upon its base, and it was set firm without being touched by human hands.
Blessed was that hour in which this took place!
The city of Mtskheta was filled with fear and joy, and rivers of tears streamed down the king, the princes, and all the people, as they sighed from their souls,
and they glorified God and called blessed Nino blessed. And many miracles took place on that day.
The first miracle. A certain Jew, blind from birth, came and approached the living pillar, and at once he received his sight and glorified God.
2. A certain royal child, eight years old, lay sick; he was a pagan. His mother brought him in faith,
laid him on a bed before the pillar of light, which was truly clothed in light, and she implored blessed Nino, saying:
"Look, my lady, on this son of mine, who has come near to death, for I know that the one you serve and preach to us is the God of gods."
Then the blessed Nino touched her hand to the life-giving pillar, laid it on the boy, and said to him:
"Do you believe in Jesus Christ, the Son of the living God, who came in the flesh for the salvation of the whole world?"
And the child said: "Yes, queen, I believe in Jesus Christ, the Savior of all created things." Then Saint Nino said to him:
"Be healed from now on, and glorify him by whose power you have been healed." And immediately the child got up as if he had felt no pain.
And great fear fell on the king and on the whole multitude of the people. And sick people with every kind of illness kept coming and being healed,
until the king made a wooden covering around the pillar and hid it from sight. And so the people touched the covering and were healed at once, and they glorified God, the worker of wonders.
And the king began to build a church in the garden with zeal and great joy.
Then the apostles came from Greece, an archbishop, priests and deacons, and they began to baptize all the people, as is written above.
I, Abiathar, was the priest to whom the priesthood had fallen by lot that year, when this blessed woman Nino came to Mtskheta.
At that time letters had come to me from Rome, from Egypt and from Babylon, from the Jews, from the priests and the scribes, in which it was written as follows:
"God has broken up the kingdom of the Jews. See, the prophets have fallen silent, for everything that the Spirit had moved them to speak has been fulfilled,
and we have been scattered over all the earth, and the Romans have taken our land under their rule, for we have sinned in every way and have angered God the Creator.
Now look at the books of Moses, who wrote all this for us: 'Whoever on earth calls himself God shall be hanged on a tree.'
Or perhaps we erred in the death of that Nazarene Jesus. For you see that in former times,
whenever our fathers sinned against God and forgot him entirely, he would give them over to a mighty ruler and to captivity.
But whenever they turned back and cried out, he would quickly deliver them from their distress. And we know from the Scriptures that this happened seven times.
But ever since they laid hands on that son of a poor stranger woman and killed him, God has lifted his hand against us;
he has broken up the kingdom, removed us from the temple of God, and utterly rejected our nation.
And now it is three hundred years since he has listened to our prayer at all, or shown us any relief.
It seems to me that that man was from heaven." And much more of this kind was written.
When I heard this, I began to question that woman Nino about Christ: where he came from, and for what reason God became man.
Then the blessed woman opened her mouth like a gushing spring and like a fountain that never runs dry.

She began from the things of eternity. She recited my own books by heart and explained them to me more fully. She roused me as one roused from sleep, and enlightened me as one who had fainted. She made me pity my fathers, and convinced me of the change of the Law,

until through her words I came to believe in Christ, the Son of God, in his Passion and his glorious Resurrection, and in his Second Coming in terror, and that he truly is the expectation of the Gentiles.
At that time my daughter and I were made worthy of the sprinkling and cleansing of sins, the font, that holy water,
which the prophet David longed for and could not attain. And again I heard the voice of the singers of the New Law,
which that same David longed for and did not reach. And I was made worthy to partake of the true flesh and blood of the Lamb of God, offered for the sins of the world,

whose taste and sight are sweet [cf. Psalm 34:8, 'taste and see']. And after this may the Lord grant my departure from the flesh, for my eyes have seen many miracles worked through Nino in Mtskheta in my days.
Now the house of Eliozi was in the western part of the city, at the gate of Mogveti [?], on the Kura river.
And there was a small shrine, their place of fasting, on which holy Nino raised the cross of Christ.
And there the children of the nobles from the heart of the city were baptized one after another by the hand of Jacob the priest and Prosilas the archdeacon.
And that place was called the Baptistery of the Nobles. And that place was greatly honored in our days, for it stood in the open field, with no buildings around it.
And in those days the Jews of Mtskheta grew very jealous of me, and they cut down the kilamo [?] tree that stood at the door of the shrine and adorned that place,
for its branches spread over the whole portico of the shrine. And they began to leave for wherever they had come from, all except the Barabeans,
of whose house fifty souls were baptized. And they settled in Mtskheta.
And King Mirian granted them a village called Tsikhe-Didi, and they were held in great honor by the king and the Christians, through the grace and teaching of blessed Nino.
And in those days letters arrived from Rome, from the holy patriarch, to blessed Nino, to King Mirian, and to all the Georgian people.
And an archdeacon of the Braj [?] was sent to offer praise and give a blessing, to receive the prayers of holy and blessed Nino, and to share in her grace.
And he carried a letter from the king of the Braj [?] to blessed Nino, for they had been baptized by her father Zabulon.
And they had heard all this from Jerusalem, Rome and Constantinople: that over that northern land
the Sun of Righteousness had spread, the Light who came from the Father, Christ. And for this reason the blessed letter had been written,
so that they might learn of those deeds and miracles, the wonders of the pillar and of the bramble bush, and the power of healing
that the archdeacon saw, and in amazement he glorified God. And he took the letters and departed.

And it came to pass, when the tree for the honored and victorious precious cross had been cut down, that a hundred men carried it upright with its branches and brought it into the city with its leaves.
And the people were amazed at how green and leafy it was in those days at the start of summer, when every other tree was dry,
while this one had all its leaves unwithered, and was fragrant and beautiful to look at. Then they set it up upright on its base at the south door of the church.
And a breeze blew from the waters, passed through the leaves of the tree and stirred its branches.
And it looked beautiful and was fragrant, like what we have heard tell of the alva [?] tree. And we cut it down on the 25th of the month of March, on a Friday.
And that tree stood for thirty-seven days, and its leaves did not change, as though it were standing on its own root at the head of the spring,
until all the trees of the forest were clothed with leaves and the fruit trees were adorned with blossoms.
Then, on the first of the month of May, these crosses were made, and on the seventh of that month they were set up by the laying on of the king's hands,
with joy and great eagerness on the part of the whole city, when they were all in the church.

And on those dark nights the multitude of the city saw it: behold, a cross of fire would come down, crowned with stars, and would stand above the church until dawn, and everyone glorified God for this.
And at dawn, just at daybreak, two stars would come out of it: one would go off to the east and the other to the west,
and the cross itself would go on standing there, shining as before, and little by little it would move away toward the Aragvi and stand on the hill of the rock,
on the upper side, near the spring that the tears of Saint Nino had made to well up, and from there it would rise up to heaven.
The whole multitude of the people saw this salvation of our God many times.
Only then did we begin to ask blessed Nino: "What is it, that a spark comes out and goes off to the east and to the west?"
And the saint said to the king and to all the people:
"Send men onto the high mountains, eastward as far as the mountains of Kakheti, and westward as far as your kingdom reaches.
And when those stars shine forth, let them see where they stop, and there set up these two crosses, as a [?] for all Christians and for the overthrow of the enemy."
And the king did so, and had the mountaintops watched without a break for ten days. This was on Friday, as Saturday was dawning, and the same sign appeared; it happened just as it always happened.
On the next day the men from the west came, the ones who had been standing on the mountains, that is, the mountain of Kvabtakhevi, and they told the king
that the star had stopped on the mountains of Tkhoti, had come down to the [?] (ergvi) of Kaspi, had stopped at a certain place, and had slowly vanished from sight.
Likewise the men from the east came and said: "We saw the star coming from here, and it stopped at the village of Bodi in the land of Kakheti."
Then blessed Nino ordered that these two crosses be carried off and that one be set up at Tkhoti, where God had shown the king his power:
"And give the other one to Salome of Ujarma, a true handmaid of Christ, and let her set it up in the city of Ujarma.
